detail.title: Plant Admin & HR Manager
detail.description:
About Origin

Origin (formerly 10xConstruction) is building general-purpose autonomous robots for US construction, taking on rising costs, safety risks and labour shortages. Our modular, multi-trade platform pairs purpose-built hardware with real-time site intelligence to work in complex environments and execute tasks precisely. Trained in high-fidelity simulation and already deployed on live sites, our robots deliver 5x faster execution, 250%+ margin expansion and significant cost savings. Join India's most talent-dense robotics team, with people from IITs, Stanford, UCLA and more.

About the Role

Origin is moving V3 robot assembly in-house in Bengaluru, growing to a 19-person plant team building 3 to 5 robots a month and scaling to 20. You will be the person who gets both sites open and legal, hires and onboards the technicians and engineers who run them, and keeps the plant compliant, staffed and running day to day. You report to the Supply Chain Lead & Plant Head and work alongside the Plant Supervisor and the Manufacturing Engineer. This is a founding, hands-on role: on day one there is a bare shed and a plan.

Key Responsibilities

Facility set-up and administration

  • Run the lease search and sign-off for the interim unit and the SEZ factory with brokers, landlords and legal: term sheet, fire NOC, electrical load, fit-out permissions, exit terms.
  • Own the fit-out schedule with the Manufacturing Engineer: contractors, racking, partitions, test rooms, mezzanine, power, internet, water and sanitation, delivered on the plan dates.
  • Run the plant day to day: security, housekeeping, canteen, transport, utilities, AMCs, consumables, visitor and vendor access, and the move from the interim unit to the SEZ factory.

Statutory compliance and licensing

  • Obtain and maintain every registration the plant needs: GST additional place of business, Shops & Establishments, trade license, Factories Act license, KSPCB consent, fire NOC, BESCOM sanction, and the SEZ/EOU or MOOWR filings with the liaison and customs consultants.
  • Own the statutory calendar: PF, ESI, professional tax, labour-welfare, contract-labour and factory returns, registers, inspections and renewals, with zero lapses.
  • Set and enforce plant safety and security routines: battery charging and storage SOPs, lifting, PPE, fire drills, incident log and first-aid readiness.

Hiring and onboarding the plant team

  • Hire the plant team to the needed-by dates on the org chart: technicians (mechanical, embedded, IQC), stores, QA, logistics and sourcing roles, through ITIs, diploma colleges, staffing agencies and referrals.
  • Run the pipeline in Workable end to end: sourcing, screening, trade tests with the Plant Supervisor, offers, background checks and joining.
  • Onboard every joiner with documentation, induction, safety briefing, uniforms and tools, and a 30-day check-in.

People operations

  • Run monthly payroll inputs, attendance, shifts, leave and overtime for the plant with Finance; keep personnel files and HRMS records accurate.
  • Handle contract-labour and agency compliance, grievances, discipline and exits with fairness and documentation.
  • Build the plant's people rhythm: skill matrix, training records, retention actions for technicians, and the engagement that keeps a 19-person floor working as one team.

Costs, vendors and records

  • Manage the plant admin budget, vendor contracts and purchase requests for admin and facilities spend; track actuals against the approved plan.
  • Keep the plant's compliance and facility documentation audit-ready for customers, auditors, customs and SEZ authorities.

Required Qualifications and Skills

  • MUST HAVE: Has set up or run plant administration and HR at a manufacturing unit in Karnataka, including the licences and registrations a factory needs to open.
  • MUST HAVE: Has hired blue-collar technicians at volume through ITIs, agencies or walk-ins, and run their onboarding and payroll compliance.
  • 4 to 8 years in plant administration, factory HR or a combined admin-HR role in an electronics, automotive, EMS or machinery plant.
  • Working knowledge of the Factories Act, Shops & Establishments Act, Contract Labour Act, PF, ESI, professional tax and KSPCB categories, and comfort dealing with inspectors and government offices in person.
  • Fluent in Kannada and English; Hindi or Tamil a plus for the technician pool.
  • Organized and documented by habit: registers, trackers and calendars that someone else could pick up tomorrow.
  • Comfortable in a bare industrial space, on your feet, solving the problem in front of you.

Preferred Experience

  • Opening a greenfield unit, or moving a plant from one site to another, on a fixed date.
  • Export-oriented or bonded premises: SEZ, EOU or MOOWR filings, customs bonding inspections, Development Commissioner liaison.
  • Workable or a similar ATS, an HRMS, and payroll tools such as GreytHR or Keka.
  • Startup or small-company environment where you were the only admin and HR person.
  • ISO 9001 or similar audit preparation for a plant.

About the role

The Stores Executive will run the stores at Origin's robot assembly plant in Bengaluru, ensuring every build starts with a complete kit and every part in stock is accounted for. The role owns the full material flow inside the plant, from the receipt of components, sub-assemblies, consumables and tooling, through quality inspection, binning and stock control, to kitting, issue to the assembly line and outbound dispatch. It also owns the stores records and processes in the inventory system and ERP. The role reports to the Plant Supervisor and works closely with Procurement, Quality Assurance, Assembly, Logistics and Finance.

Key Responsibilities

  • Receive inbound consignments against the purchase order, verify quantities and documents, route every receipt through the Quality Assurance team for inspection, and raise the GRN once material is cleared; report shortages, damages or mismatches to Procurement for resolution.
  • Segregate rejected and non-conforming material, issue rejection notes, and coordinate vendor returns and replacements with Procurement and Quality Assurance.
  • Organize the stores with a defined bin-location system, FIFO practice, ESD-safe storage for electronics, dedicated storage for lithium-ion batteries, and clear separation of inspected, pending, rejected and returned stock.
  • Maintain inventory accuracy of 99% or higher through regular cycle counts and periodic physical verification, reconciling every variance.
  • Plan stock levels by part category in line with the production plan and supplier lead times, and raise material requirements to Procurement well in advance to prevent line stoppages.
  • Prepare complete kits for each assembly stage from released work orders ahead of the production schedule, identifying shortages early and escalating them to Procurement and the Assembly team with clear priority and required-by dates.
  • Issue kits, consumables and tooling to the assembly line with documented acknowledgement, receive unused, surplus and defective material back, and keep consumption, scrap and rework records accurate against each work order.
  • Pack and document outbound movements, including finished robots and spares for export, parts sent to vendors for rework or calibration, and supplier returns, with complete challans, packing lists, e-way bills and GST documentation.
  • Maintain item masters, GRNs, issue records and the stock ledger in the inventory system and ERP, support the rollout of stores workflows, and share a weekly update with the Plant Supervisor on inventory health, kit readiness, upcoming shortages, slow-moving stock and open rejections.
  • Coordinate with stores assistants and material handlers on daily receiving and issue, and uphold safety and housekeeping through 5S, material handling equipment checks, battery storage SOPs and PPE compliance, with documented SOPs for every stores process.

Required Qualifications and Skills

  • Diploma or Bachelor's degree in Mechanical, Electrical, Electronics or Industrial Engineering, Materials Management, Supply Chain or a related field.
  • 2–4 years of experience in stores or warehouse operations at a manufacturing plant, preferably electronics, automotive, EMS or machinery.
  • Experience issuing material to a production line against BOMs or work orders.
  • Working knowledge of GRN, delivery challan and e-way bill documentation.
  • Ability to read a BOM and identify mechanical, electrical and electronic components.
  • Hands-on with an ERP or inventory system and comfortable with Google Sheets or Excel.

Preferred Experience

  • Stores experience in a plant that builds complex, low-volume assemblies such as robotics, EVs, drones, aerospace, medical devices, defense or capital equipment.
  • Exposure to ISO 9001 or similar audits covering material traceability.
  • Experience with barcode or QR-based stock tracking and handheld scanners for receiving, picking and counting.
  • Familiarity with lean stores practices such as visual stock controls and point-of-use replenishment for the assembly line.
  • Experience managing tools and consumables issue through a tool crib or similar system.

detail.title: Founding AI Research Engineer - Robot Learning
detail.description:
About Origin

Origin is building Physical AI for the built world - starting with autonomous robots for Interior Construction. We are building Construction Action Models which allows our modular robots to learn, adapt and work in unstructured construction job site.

Our robots are already deployed on live sites in New York City, helping accelerate schedules for large-scale commercial projects while improving safety and predictability on the job site. Backed by Tier-1 investors, Origin is working to close the gap between America’s surging demand for housing, data centers, and manufacturing infrastructure, and the construction industry’s growing labor shortage.

The Role

Our system runs a Multi Agent Action Expert architecture: classical precision algorithms orchestrated alongside learned policies. The job is systematically expanding the learned components while keeping the system production-safe. You own the full lifecycle of learned components on OG-1: from data collection and model training through edge deployment on Jetson AGX Orin. Every research project will have a deployment milestone. This is not a lab position.

What You Will Do

  • Train and deploy VLA models for contact-rich manipulation using our imitation learning infrastructure.
  • Build the data flywheel: teleoperation pipelines (GELLO, SpaceMouse, VR), DAgger-style online correction, demonstration curation.
  • Research and prototype world models for surface state prediction, spray dynamics, and anomaly detection.
  • Design offline evaluation metrics that predict real-world finishing quality before deployment.
  • Optimize models for edge: TensorRT compilation, latency profiling, memory budgeting on dual Jetson AGX Orin.
  • Design the interface where learned policies propose actions and deterministic safety layers enforce constraints.
detail.requirements:
• BS/MS/PhD in CS, Robotics, ML, or equivalent experience shipping learned systems on physical robots.
  • Strong Python and PyTorch; comfort modifying research codebases (you'll work directly with open-source VLA implementations).
  • Experience in at least two of: imitation learning, RL, vision-language models, robot learning from demonstration, sim-to-real.
  • Track record deploying ML on real hardware: not just training to convergence, but debugging why the policy fails on the actual robot.
  • Working knowledge of ROS2 or equivalent robotics middleware.
  • Experience working with Simulation Systems like Isaac Sim.
  • GPU profiling and optimization (TensorRT, ONNX, CUDA); you understand why 200ms policy latency kills contact control.

Strong Plus

  • Hands-on with VLA architectures (π0/π0.5, OpenVLA, RT-2, Octo) or foundation model fine-tuning for robotics.
  • Teleoperation data collection and DAgger/HG-DAgger pipelines.
  • World model architectures (DreamerV3, V-JEPA, latent dynamics models).
  • Construction, manufacturing, or contact-rich industrial domains.
  • Publications at CoRL, RSS, ICRA, NeurIPS: valued but equivalent shipped work counts.

About the role

Robotic drywall finishing is a hard, unsolved problem, and progress depends on how many good experiments we can run. As an apprentice, you will spend most of your time on the robot: setting up trials, running DOEs on the spraying and sanding process, and turning results into findings that engineering decisions can rest on.

Because you will run the same protocols again and again, you will see better than anyone where the manual effort goes. Your second job is to measure that effort and tell us, with numbers, what to automate next, and to build the simpler automations yourself.

The work is deliberately interdisciplinary: robot, sensors, wiring, scripts and experimental method in the same week. If you think like an experimentalist and are comfortable with a wrench in one hand and a terminal in the other, this role is for you.

What you will do
Run experiments on the robot (most of your time)

  • Run controlled experiments on robotic drywall finishing processes using hypothesis-driven and DOE-based approaches.
  • Identify and isolate independent, dependent, controlled and confounding variables across physical trials.
  • Maintain repeatability and reproducibility discipline in measurement; know the difference between a real effect and setup noise.
  • Analye cross-system interactions across the robot arm, end-effector, sensors, surface material and motion parameters.
  • Convert trial results into clear experiment logs, test reports and result summaries.

Keep setups trial-ready

  • Assemble, wire, calibrate and maintain the rigs, fixtures and end-of-arm tooling used in your trials, working with the robotics team.
  • Debug setup problems across mechanical, electrical and software layers and keep setups in a known-good state.

Find and drive automation

  • Time each step of the experiment cycle and find where hours are lost between "run the trial" and "read the result".
  • Propose automations for test protocols (motion sequences, parameter sweeps, data capture, logging, first-pass analysis), ranked by time saved.
  • Build the simpler ones in Python (and ROS 2 as you learn it), and write clear specs for the larger ones so the robotics team can build them.

About the role

As a Mechanical QA Tester, you will carry out mechanical inspection and validation testing on robot components, sub-assemblies and complete robots. You will follow test plans and procedures written by the Mechanical QA Engineer, take accurate measurements, run durability and environmental tests, and report every failure clearly. Your work helps make sure each robot can survive demanding construction-site use. You will report to the Mechanical QA Engineer and work closely with the mechanical design, manufacturing and assembly teams.

Key responsibilities

Run validation tests

  • Run structural, endurance, vibration, shock, ingress (dust and water), thermal and abuse tests by following the written procedure step by step.
  • Set up test fixtures, rigs and sensors, and mount robots or assemblies on them safely before each run.
  • Monitor tests while they run, record cycle counts, readings and observations, and stop the test if a safety or damage limit is reached.
  • Run automated test-rig sequences from a laptop or HMI using written steps.

Inspect parts and assemblies

  • Measure parts with vernier calipers, micrometers, height gauges, dial indicators, feeler gauges and other inspection tools.
  • Check dimensions, fitment, alignment and surface condition against drawings and inspection checklists.
  • Verify fastener torque with torque wrenches, and check welds, paint or coating, and sealing.
  • Support incoming, in-process and end-of-line quality checks on the shop floor.
  • Record all measurements on inspection sheets and mark out-of-tolerance values.

Report failures

  • Log each failure or non-conformance in the test management tool with the test ID, part or unit serial number, observed result, expected result, measurements and photos or video.
  • Flag safety issues and blocking failures to the QA lead immediately.
  • Keep failed parts tagged and set aside for root-cause analysis.
  • Retest units after fixes and close the related reports.

General

  • Follow PPE, lifting, lockout and machine safety rules at all times, especially around heavy robots and moving mechanisms.
  • Keep inspection tools, fixtures and the test area organised, clean and in calibration.
  • Suggest clearer test steps or better fixtures when a procedure is confusing, slow or out of date.

All candidates must show solid, hands-on competency in every item below. Expect each one to be tested in the interview.

• Git from the command line: branching, merging, rebasing, and resolving conflicts.

• Ability to learn independently by reading man pages, documentation, datasheets, and RFCs.

Good to Have
• Exposure to ROS 2 (pub/sub, services, actions, launch files) or DDS.
• Familiarity with CMake (targets, find_package, CTest).
• Understanding of P2P vs. centralized messaging (e.g. DDS vs. MQTT).
• Network configuration on routers and switches, including VLANs.
• Basic knowledge of SQL or NoSQL databases.
• Basics of network security: checksums and hashes (CRC, SHA), public-key encryption, and digital signatures.
• Projects on embedded hardware (Jetson, Raspberry Pi) or self-hosted servers and home networks.
• Open-source contributions or a GitHub profile showing systems-level work.

What You'll Get
• Close mentorship from senior platform and robotics engineers, with regular code reviews and 1:1s.
• Real ownership of production systems running on robots deployed on live construction sites.
• Broad exposure across embedded Linux, networking, middleware, and cloud infrastructure.

detail.title: Marketing Lead
detail.description:
About Origin

Origin (previously 10xConstruction) is building general-purpose autonomous robots for US construction to tackle rising costs, safety risks, and labour shortages. About the Role

As Marketing Lead, you will own how Origin is understood by contractors, developers, partners, press, and investors, and build the marketing function that turns that understanding into demand for OG1.

Construction robotics is an understood category. Origin's position inside it is not: one general-purpose robot that performs every interior-finishing trade starting with compound application, sanding, priming, and painting and adding other interior workflows, in a market conditioned to expect a separate machine for each task. Making that idea land is patient, repeated work, and it is the core of this role.

You will define the positioning, build the awareness engine behind it, stand up always-on demand generation that produces qualified conversations, find and win the stages where a working robot deserves to be seen, and hold every internal department and external agencies and partners to one visual and verbal system.

Because Origin sells across India, the United States, Europe, and Asia Pacific, you will also build a marketing plan for each region rather than one global plan that fits none of them. You will have a Creative Content Producer working to your plan, alongside creative, content, and PR agencies and freelancers, and you will be the person who keeps all of them pointed at the same narrative and coordinated around the same release calendar. For the first year you are the marketing team: you will set the strategy and you will also fix the product page, write the brief, and staff the booth.

What You'll Do

1. Positioning and Category Awareness

-        Define Origin's category position, the proof behind it, what it displaces, and what it is routinely confused with.

-        Build audience-specific message tracks for general contractors, interior and drywall subcontractors, developers and owners, partners, press, and investors.

-        Run a sustained awareness plan of explainers, demonstrations, comparisons, briefings, and formats that move audiences from "a robot that plasters and paints" to "a platform that does all interior works."

-        Write and maintain objection handling for the questions that decide deals, including why a general-purpose platform beats single-task machines and manual crews.

-        Test messaging in real sales calls, pilots, partner meetings, and investor conversations, and change it on evidence rather than opinion.

-        Keep one approved boilerplate, product description, and narrative live across the website, decks, brochures, outbound, job postings, and investor material.

-        Build named, repeatable formats Origin owns outright, a series people subscribe to rather than stumble across, instead of campaigns that end and leave nothing behind.

-        Hold the line that renders explain and footage proves: claims about OG1 are backed by real site evidence, because the buyer has been sold construction robotics before and it did not work.

2. Demand Generation

-        Build always-on channels with playbooks, owners, budgets, and locked measurement, so pipeline does not depend on the event calendar.

-        Run a monthly campaign rhythm with documented experiments covering hypothesis, result, learning, and decision.

-        Own the website and product pages as working sales surfaces, not brochures.

-        Make Origin the source AI answer engines quote: canonical explainers targeting what a contractor actually asks, structured for search and for generative answers rather than written as keyword filler.

-        Own tracking, source capture, UTM discipline, and attribution hygiene end to end.

-        Report qualified conversations and cost per qualified conversation by channel and by region.

-        Route inbound enquiries to Sales quickly, with source, segment, and region recorded.

3. Events, Showcases, and Industry Presence

-        Own the showcase portfolio across trade shows, pavilions, speaking slots, panels, awards, innovation programme, demo days, customer and partner site demonstrations, industry bodies, press and analyst briefings, and investor events.

-        Actively hunt for opportunities Origin is not already tracking, and qualify each on audience fit, buyer density, cost, and effort before committing.

-        Work every membership and sponsorship Origin already pays for until it delivers the visibility it promised.

-        Write and submit speaking abstracts, panel proposals, and award nominations against a tracked deadline calendar.

-        Run each committed appearance to a written brief agreed with the internal team and the event coordinator, covering objective, demo plan, staffing, collateral, lead capture, and follow-up ownership.

-        Score every paid appearance against cost within thirty days, and make the renewal recommendation from that number.

4. Brand, Design, and Messaging Consistency

-        Publish and maintain Origin's brand and messaging system, covering logo and colour usage, typography, imagery and robot photography standards, diagram conventions, templates, product naming, and approved terminology.

-        Roll the system out to Sales, Engineering, Hardware, Deployment, People, and leadership with the templates each team actually needs.

-        Review externally published technical material for terminology and message consistency without dulling its technical accuracy.

-        Make the compliant path the easy one through templates and a fast request route, rather than policing after the fact.

-        Keep design, messaging, and product naming consistent across web, decks, documents, event collateral, site signage, and technical documentation.

5. Product Marketing, Launches, and Campaign Coordination

-        Build the launch playbook and run it on OG1 milestones, from positioning and proof through assets, channels, internal readiness, and post-launch review.

-        Own the release calendar and coordinate every party against it — the Creative Content Producer, creative and content agencies, PR support, Sales, Deployment, and Engineering — so product milestones, content, events, and announcements land together rather than separately.

-        Write the single narrative brief that the content team, agencies, and freelancers all work from, so one campaign does not arrive in three different voices.

-        Run the approval and review flow for campaigns and releases, with clear owners, deadlines, and a final sign-off that does not sit with the founders by default.

-        Equip Sales with the enterprise kit before they ask: pitch narrative, RaaS economics and ROI material, pilot evidence, case studies, compliance one-pagers, and the objection library.

-        Maintain competitive positioning and comparison material against other construction robotics players and manual alternatives.

-        Support fundraising and partnership conversations with accurate, current narrative material.

6. Regional Marketing

-        Write and run a marketing plan for each active market, covering the local buyer, the labor-cost and ROI argument, the competitive set, regulatory message constraints, localization, channel mix, local events, and partner support.

-        Localize messaging rather than translating it, and validate it in-market before scaling.

-        Report each region against its own baseline and recommend where budget should move.

7. Founder Voice and Employee-Generated Content

-        Run the founder-voice programme: three co-founders with genuinely distinct public voices and distinct territory — company thesis, autonomy and physical AI, hardware reality — supported to publish on a cadence without being flattened into one house tone.

-        Build and run an employee-generated content programme across deployment, operations and engineering, with voice guides, prompt packs, capture kits, and an approval flow simple enough that nobody has to be a writer.

-        Keep the trust hierarchy straight: a post from a deployment lead on a live site does something a company page structurally cannot, and the programme should be designed around that.

8. Working With the Content Team, Agencies, and Partners

-        Direct the Creative Content Producer against a quarterly plan tied to the awareness, launch, and demand priorities, and make sure they walk into a running system rather than a blank calendar.

-        Select, brief, review, and manage creative, content, video, PR, and design agencies and freelancers against a defined standard, a budget, and an agreed set of deliverables.

-        Coordinate in-house and external creative on the same campaign without duplicated work or conflicting narratives, including where an agency owns production and Origin owns the message.

-        Hold external partners to measurable outcomes, review performance on a set cadence, and make the renew, renegotiate, or end call on evidence.

-        Work daily with founders, engineers, deployment, and sales to find the strongest stories and get them out quickly, and support each founder's public voice without flattening it into one house tone.

Must-Haves

-        Five or more years in B2B marketing, including time owning the function, its number, and its budget rather than a single channel within someone else's plan.

-        Demonstrated product marketing experience: you have taken a product to market, not only run campaigns for one.

-        A track record of positioning work that outlasted you — messaging other people adopted and repeated.

-        Proven ownership of demand generation against a pipeline number, with the ability to state your cost per qualified conversation without a week's preparation.

-        Experience marketing to enterprise buyers with committee decisions and multi-month sales cycles.

-        Ability to work hands-on and strategically at the same time, in a company where there is no one else to hand the work to.

-        Strong writing: you can produce a positioning document, a launch plan, a one-pager, and a conference abstract yourself.

-        Comfort with analytics, tracking, attribution, CRM, and marketing automation, and the discipline to keep the data clean.

-        Ability to hold your own with engineers, get a technical claim right, and make a complex physical product clear without flattening it.

-        The discipline to market on evidence rather than claims, to a buyer who has been promised this before: you reach for proof from real sites ahead of a better-looking render, and you can tell the difference between marketing that argues with doubt and marketing that removes the reason for it.

-        Comfort enabling other people's voices — founders, engineers, operators — rather than putting everything through a single corporate channel.

-        Experience running events or field marketing as a pipeline channel, not as logistics.

-        Experience directing creative people and external agencies against a defined standard, and coordinating in-house and outsourced creative on the same release without the work colliding.

-        Experience running a release or campaign calendar across several teams and holding it, including the unglamorous coordination that makes a launch land on one day rather than over three weeks.

-        Comfort working around engineers, hardware, robots, workshops, labs, testing areas, and live construction sites.

-        Willingness to travel domestically and internationally, including to customer sites and trade shows.

-        Genuine interest in robotics, construction, startups, and physical products.

Good-to-Haves

-        Experience marketing a physical product in robotics, hardware, manufacturing, automotive, construction technology, industrial automation, or aerospace.

-        Experience selling into construction, real estate, infrastructure, or field-service buyers.

-        Experience marketing a subscription, leasing, or as-a-service commercial model.

-        Experience building a brand and design system that technical teams actually adopted.

-        Experience running marketing across more than one country or region, including localization.

-        Experience with account-based marketing against a named target list.

-        Experience building a category or evangelizing an unfamiliar product class.

-        Experience supporting fundraising with narrative and investor-facing material.

-        Experience working with press, analysts, or industry associations.

-        Experience on the client side of an agency relationship — scoping, briefing, and getting real output from a narrative, content, or PR partner.

-        Experience with AI-assisted marketing tooling used for real leverage rather than novelty.

-        Familiarity with construction workflows, jobsites, and industrial environments.

Application Requirement

Applicants must share examples of their own work: a positioning or messaging document, a launch plan, a campaign with its results, or a piece of enablement material you wrote.

We are especially interested in work involving technical or physical products, unfamiliar product categories, enterprise buyers, and results you can attribute to your own decisions.

Shortlisted candidates will be asked to complete a short practical assignment on positioning and launching OG1.

What You'll Gain

-        The opportunity to define the category position of an early-stage robotics company, rather than inherit one.

-        Ownership of an entire marketing function, its budget, and its first hires.

-        Direct work with founders, engineers, robots, customer demonstrations, and field deployments.

-        Experience marketing a physical, AI-driven product into one of the world's largest and least digitized industries.

-        Exposure across sales, fundraising, partnerships, and product as marketing touches all of them.

-        International scope from day one, across India, the United States, Europe, and Asia Pacific.

Subsystem Design & Analysis:

  • Develop and execute rigorous physical Verification and Validation (V&V) protocols (e.g., drop testing, vibration tables, and continuous load cycling).
  • Own the DFMEA for your subsystems and implement design changes to mitigate identified failure modes.

Real-to-Virtual Fidelity:

  • Create and maintain mathematically rigorous URDFs for your subsystems, calculating exact inertial properties, centre of mass, and friction models to feed the simulation and controls teams.

Prototyping & Mentorship:

  • Lead rapid prototyping efforts to physically validate designs before committing to expensive tooling.
  • Mentor junior engineers in CAD best practices, FEA setups, and GD&T application.

  • 4-8 years of professional experience in designing dynamic mechanical systems.
  • Expert proficiency in CAD software (Onshape or equivalent) and PDM systems.
  • Strong background in applying GD&T (ASME Y14.5) and performing complex 3D tolerance stack-up analyses.
  • Deep understanding of material science, metal fabrication (machining, welding, casting), and structural mechanics.

detail.description:
About Origin

About the role


Robotic drywall finishing is a hard, unsolved problem — and you'll be in the thick of solving it.
This role sits at the intersection of three things: building the physical setups we experiment on, running the experiments that tell us what actually works, and automating those experiments so we can run far more of them. You'll stand up test rigs and instrumentation, design and execute DOEs on the robotic finishing process, and then write the ROS 2 and Python tooling that turns a manual trial into a repeatable, scripted protocol.
It is deliberately interdisciplinary — mechanical assembly, embedded systems and sensors, robot software, and experimental method all in the same week. We're looking for someone whose experience is broad rather than narrow: two years spent solving a variety of problems across several projects teaches you more of what this role needs than two years spent deep inside a single one.
If you think like an experimentalist, are comfortable with a wrench in one hand and a terminal in the other, and want your work to visibly move the system forward, this role is for you.


Key Responsibilities


Build and maintain experimental setups

  • Design, build, instrument, and maintain test rigs, fixtures, and experimental setups for robotic drywall finishing trials
  • Integrate sensors, end-of-arm (EOA) tooling, actuators, and data acquisition hardware into working setups; own wiring, mounting, calibration, and day-to-day upkeep
  • Debug setups end to end across mechanical, electrical, embedded, and software layers, and keep them in a known-good, repeatable state
  • Improve setup design over time so experiments get faster, cleaner, and easier to reproduce

Design and run experiments

  • Design and run controlled experiments on robotic drywall finishing processes using hypothesis-driven and DOE-based approaches
  • Identify and isolate independent, dependent, controlled, and confounding variables across physical trials
  • Maintain repeatability and reproducibility discipline in measurement workflows; know the difference between a real effect and setup noise
  • Analyse cross-system interactions across the robot arm, end-effector, sensors, surface material, and motion parameters to support debugging and process improvement
  • Document observations rigorously and convert trial results into clear experiment logs, test reports, and result summaries that engineering decisions can be based on

Automate test protocols

  • Automate test and measurement protocols using ROS 2 and Python to increase the rate of experimentation
  • Script robot motion sequences, parameter sweeps, and data capture so trials run consistently with minimal manual intervention
  • Build tooling for automated data collection, logging, and first-pass analysis; reduce the manual effort between "run the trial" and "read the result"
  • Work with the robotics team on deep data collection from EOA systems with advanced sensors — from wiring and drivers through to structured, analysable datasets

Required Qualifications and Skills

  • B.E./B.Tech/M.E./M.Tech in Mechanical, Mechatronics, Robotics, Electrical/Electronics, Instrumentation, Industrial, Aerospace, or Systems Engineering (candidates from Applied Sciences / Experimental Physics with strong hands-on engineering exposure may also be considered)
  • ~2 years of hands-on experience in the robotics and automation field, across a variety of solutioning-driven projects. Breadth matters here: we value someone who has shipped several different builds, integrations, or test systems over someone who has spent the same period on one narrow scope
  • Demonstrated experimentation experience in a lab, R&D, or test-engineering environment — designing trials, not just executing someone else's checklist
  • Working knowledge of ROS 2 (nodes, topics, launch files, basic packages) and comfort writing production-quality-enough Python for automation, data capture, and analysis
  • Basics of embedded systems — microcontrollers, sensor interfacing, common protocols (UART/I2C/SPI/CAN), and the ability to read a datasheet and get a sensor talking
  • Hands-on competence with electromechanical assemblies, sensors, instrumentation, wiring, and calibration
  • Understanding of experimental methods, statistics/DOE, control systems, and system design through coursework, research, or industry work
  • Ability to work with engineering data from physical trials and perform statistical analysis and interpretation
  • Strong documentation skills — structured test reports, experiment logs, and result summaries
  • Genuine appetite to learn across disciplines, and comfort working on an unsolved problem where the right answer isn't known yet

Preferred Experience

  • Experience with industrial or collaborative robot arms — UR, KUKA, ABB, Fanuc, or similar — including motion programming and integration
  • Prior work with imaging-based experimentation setups (computer vision, machine vision, optical or laser-based measurement)
  • Experience designing test setups, instrumentation chains, or validation workflows from scratch
  • Force/torque sensing, IMUs, depth cameras, encoders, or other advanced sensing integrated into a working data pipeline
  • Familiarity with data acquisition systems, real-time logging, or time-synchronised multi-sensor capture
  • Comfort with Excel/Google Sheets, Python (NumPy/pandas/matplotlib), or MATLAB for experiment logging, analysis, and plotting
  • Exposure to CAD tools (SolidWorks / Fusion 360 / Onshape) for designing fixtures and brackets
  • Version control (Git) and documentation tools (Notion, Confluence, Jira, or Google Docs)
  • Exposure to simulation environments (Gazebo, Isaac Sim) or process/materials domains such as coatings, surface finishing, or abrasives

Why this role


You will own the loop between a physical question and a defensible answer — building the rig, running the experiment, and automating it so the next hundred runs are cheap. The scope is broad by design, the feedback is fast, and the results go straight into a robot working on live construction sites.

detail.description:

Our priority is the buildout the US cannot afford to slow down: data centres and power plants, where rising costs, safety risks, and labour shortages hit hardest. As Creative Content Producer, you will shape how Origin tells its story across video, social media, visual design, presentations, and brand assets.

You will capture content from our lab, office, robot testing, demos, team activities, deployment preparation, customer engagements, and field operations. You will also turn footage from international deployments, pilots, trade shows, and customer sites into compelling content.

This is more than a video-editing role. You will make complex, physical, real-world technology feel clear, credible, and exciting to customers, investors, partners, candidates, and the construction industry.

Because you will not always be where the action happens, you will also build simple, repeatable systems that help field teams around the world capture high-quality and usable content.

  • Own video projects from ideation and scripting through shooting, editing, packaging, and publishing support.
  • Produce short- and long-form content for LinkedIn, Instagram, YouTube, X, and other relevant channels.
  • Create product demos, robot showcases, explainers, reels, founder and team videos, behind-the-scenes stories, launch videos, event recaps, and deployment updates.

  • Turn complex robotics, construction workflows, product capabilities, and field learnings into clear and engaging stories.
  • Adapt content for customers, investors, partners, candidates, and technical audiences.

  • Support time-sensitive content needs from international customer demos, pilots, deployments, trade shows, and site visits.
  • Create shot lists, filming guides, interview prompts, capture checklists, and content-request templates.
  • Guide engineers, operators, salespeople, and deployment teams in capturing better video, photography, interviews, and customer moments.
  • Turn raw field footage into reels, demo highlights, customer-facing clips, case-study assets, sales materials, investor updates, and internal communications.
  • Build a repeatable field-content system for documenting robot performance, jobsite workflows, customer reactions, and deployment learnings.

3. Visual and Brand Design

  • Create reusable templates for social posts, video thumbnails, announcements, presentations, case studies, and launches.
  • Maintain visual consistency across video, social media, web, presentations, and print.
  • Support visuals for landing pages, product showcases, and campaign pages when needed.

4. Collaboration and Brand Storytelling

  • Work closely with founders, engineers, product, deployment, sales, and marketing teams to identify content opportunities.
  • Interview and film team members, operators, customers, and leadership.
  • Help construction companies understand how Origin’s robots work, where they fit, and why they matter.
  • Build a credible, high-trust brand grounded in real products, real progress, and real-world performance.
  • Help teams recognize what should be captured and how it can become valuable content.

Must-Haves

  • A strong portfolio or showreel demonstrating video production, editing, visual design, or social content.
  • Ability to independently take video projects from idea and scripting through shooting, editing, and final delivery.
  • Strong proficiency with at least one video-editing tool, such as Adobe Premiere Pro, Final Cut Pro, DaVinci Resolve, or CapCut.
  • Working proficiency with design tools such as Figma, Photoshop, Illustrator, Canva, or equivalent.
  • A strong eye for storytelling, framing, composition, pacing, typography, layout, and visual hierarchy.
  • Ability to create both polished brand content and fast, platform-native social content.
  • Familiarity with LinkedIn, Instagram Reels, YouTube, YouTube Shorts, and emerging content formats.
  • Ability to simplify technical subjects into clear and visually engaging stories.
  • Confidence turning imperfect or remotely captured footage into high-quality content.
  • Comfort working around engineers, hardware, robots, workshops, labs, testing areas, and field operations.
  • Ability to guide non-creative colleagues in capturing usable photos, videos, interviews, and customer moments.
  • Strong ownership, organization, resourcefulness, and ability to manage several creative projects at once.
  • Willingness to occasionally appear on camera.
  • Genuine interest in robotics, construction, technology, startups, and physical products.

Good-to-Haves

  • Experience in robotics, hardware, manufacturing, automotive, construction technology, industrial automation, aerospace, or another physical-product industry.
  • Experience working with engineering, product, deployment, sales, or other technical teams.
  • Experience producing content from customer sites, factories, labs, workshops, trade shows, or international deployments.
  • Experience building remote content-capture systems using shot lists, filming guides, prompts, checklists, and reusable templates.
  • Experience creating founder-led or technical content for LinkedIn.
  • Motion graphics, animation, 3D visualization, product-rendering, or interface-animation skills.
  • Photography skills, including lighting, framing, composition, and image editing.
  • Experience creating pitch decks, sales materials, case studies, one-pagers, event collateral, thumbnails, or product explainers.
  • Understanding of brand identity systems and cross-channel visual consistency.
  • Experience creating reusable workflows and templates that help teams publish consistently.
  • Familiarity with construction workflows, jobsites, industrial environments, or B2B technology audiences.

Portfolio Requirement

Applicants must share a portfolio, show reel, social media samples, design work, or links to published videos.

We are especially interested in technical storytelling, hardware or product videos, founder-led content, social videos, motion graphics, brand design, and work involving physical products.

Shortlisted candidates may be asked to complete a small practical assignment using sample robot footage.

What You’ll Gain

  • The opportunity to shape the creative voice of an early-stage robotics company.
  • Hands-on experience with robotics, AI, automation, construction technology, and physical products.
  • A diverse portfolio spanning video, design, technical storytelling, product launches, and brand campaigns.
  • Direct exposure to founders, engineers, robots, customer demonstrations, and field deployments.
  • Experience creating content that supports sales, hiring, fundraising, brand development, and product adoption.
  • The chance to tell the story of technology being built for one of the world’s largest industries.

About the Role


You will work on building and optimizing 3D perception systems that enable robots to understand and interact with complex real-world environments. The goal is to develop robust perception pipelines that work reliably across both simulation and real-world construction sites, ensuring accurate scene understanding, localization, and decision-making.

Key Responsibilities


3D Perception Development & Scene Understanding

  • Design, implement, and deploy realtime 3D perception pipelines leveraging LiDAR, IMU, Stereo, and RGB cameras.
  • Develop algorithms for spatial and temporal data interpretation to enable high-fidelity semantic scene understanding.
  • Optimize ego-motion estimation and localization modules to ensure seamless integration with downstream planning and control tasks.



Deep Learning

  • Train and integrate deep learning models required for semantic world understanding and surface finish classification for quality control
  • Collect and curate high-quality datasets (real and synthetic) and automate training pipelines and experiment tracking.
  • Benchmark and optimize perception models for edge devices to ensure real-time performance in resource-constrained environments



Sensor Fusion & Localization

  • Design and implement sensor fusion strategies combining visual, inertial, and spatial data
  • Architect and implement sophisticated sensor fusion strategies that integrate classical methods with deep learning approaches to convert noisy, asynchronous data from heterogeneous sensors into a unified environment representation.



Calibration

  • Develop and automate robust extrinsic and intrinsic calibration procedures (Camera, LiDAR, IMU) using target-based and/or targetless methods.
  • Design and implement algorithms for online calibration drift detection and self-healing to maintain system integrity during long-term deployments.
  • Establish rigorous quantitative metrics to objectively evaluate and certify calibration quality.



Collaboration

  • Partner with Navigation, Manipulation, and Cloud teams to ensure perception outputs are optimized for downstream path planning, grasping, and remote fleet monitoring.
  • Define, track system-level and own system level KPIs and perception metrics to identify regressions across software iterations.

  • 5+ YoE

  • Proficiency in C++ (Python is a plus)

Nice to Have

  • Experience with ROS/ROS2

  • Familiarity with OpenCV, PCL, or similar libraries
  • Experience working on robotics or vision-based projects

About the role

As the Lead Embedded Hardware and Power Engineer, you will own the end-to-end electrical architecture of our heavy-duty autonomous robots. You will architect the high-power systems capable of running demanding construction end-effectors all day, as well as the intricate embedded hardware that drives our compute and control stacks. You will make the definitive decisions on system topology, safety architectures, and regulatory compliance, guiding the hardware team from white-board concepts to mass manufacturing.

Key Responsibilities

System Architecture & Strategy:

  • Define the global electrical and power topology for the robot, balancing high-power demands with the strict noise requirements of sensitive compute and perception sensors.
  • Architect custom Battery Management Systems (BMS), high-power inverters, and fast-charging systems tailored for rugged construction environments.

Advanced Hardware Design & HIL Strategy:

  • Lead the schematic design and review process for all custom PCBs (using Altium/Eagle), focusing on high-current routing, thermal management, and EMI/EMC mitigation.
  • Define the global Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) testing strategy, architecting simulation environments that validate functional safety and system reliability before physical deployment.
  • Design complex, high-reliability wire harness architectures.

Hardware Defined-Safety Systems:

  • Architect the global hardware-based safety loop, integrating error signals (e.g., over-current faults, thermal limiters, hardware watchdogs) from distributed compute and motor drives into a centralized, fail-safe E-stop circuit. 
  • Ensure the entire hardware safety topology complies with industrial standards (e.g., ISO 13849, IEC 61508) independently of software state.

Compliance & Manufacturing:

  • Drive the product through rigorous regulatory approval processes (UL, CE, FCC), acting as the primary technical authority for compliance testing.
  • Manage relationships with contract manufacturers (CMs) and define the end-of-line (EOL) testing strategy for PCBs and assembled power systems.

Leadership:

  • Mentor and lead a team of hardware engineers, establishing strict guidelines for design reviews, component selection, and testing protocols.

Required Qualifications and Skills

  • Master's degree in Electrical/Electronics Engineering, Robotics, or a related field.
  • 8+ years of deep experience in embedded hardware, power electronics, and high-voltage DC/AC systems.
  • Expert-level proficiency in PCB design software (Altium Designer preferred).
  • Extensive experience navigating regulatory approval processes (UL, CE, FCC) for heavy electronics.
  • Deep knowledge of EMI/EMC mitigation techniques in mixed-signal and high-power boards.
  • Strong understanding of industrial communication buses (CAN, Ethernet, SPI, I2C) at the hardware level.

Preferred Experiences

  • Experience in the EV (Electric Vehicle), aerospace, or heavy machinery industries.
  • Experience designing systems to functional safety standards.

detail.description:
About Origin

About the role

The Logistics & Freight Manager will build and run Origin's global import and export operations to enable production as per the manufacturing plan and the movement of finished robots to live construction sites across the countries in Pipeline. The role owns end-to-end freight execution across air, ocean, and in-land modes — inbound components, sub-assemblies, and capital equipment from suppliers across India, China, Taiwan, South-East Asia, the US, and Europe; outbound robots, spares, and RMA units to customer sites and overseas entities. It also owns the customs, documentation, and trade compliance layer beneath both flows, along with forwarder and customs-broker management, freight rate negotiation, and freight spend. This role acts as the commercial and compliance bridge between Supply Chain, Mechanical and Electrical Engineering, Production, Finance, and the US deployment team.

Key Responsibilities

● Own end-to-end import operations — shipment planning, booking, document validation, customs clearance, and final delivery to plant or warehouse — for components, sub-assemblies, tooling, and capital equipment.

● Own end-to-end export operations including shipping bill filing, certificates of origin, and destination-specific certification for US and other markets.

● Manage customs clearance through CHA partners — bill of entry filing, duty assessment, examination, out-of-charge — and drive clearance cycle time to under 3 days from document handover, with zero avoidable holds.

● Own HS classification for all BOM items and finished goods; maintain a governed, auditable classification master and ensure correct duty determination (BCD, IGST, cess, anti-dumping, FTA preferential rates with valid origin documentation).

● Maintain regulatory registrations and filings — IEC, AD Code registration at all working ports and ICDs, DGFT and ICEGATE transactions, licences and authorisations — and keep an audit-ready record set for every consignment.

● Evaluate and administer duty-saving and deferment schemes — Advance Authorisation, EPCG, MOOWR bonded manufacturing, RoDTEP, duty drawback — and track benefit realised against entitlement.

● Own dangerous goods movement for lithium-ion battery packs and battery-powered equipment — UN 38.3 test summaries, IATA DGR and IMDG documentation, packing instructions, and DG-certified forwarder selection.

● Define export packaging and crating standards for high-value, fragile, and oversized equipment — lashing, shock and tilt indicators, moisture protection — and drive zero transit damage on robot dispatches.

● Build and manage the partner panel across all modes — 3–5 evaluated freight forwarders, customs house agents, transporters, and courier partners per mode — through structured RFQs, rate benchmarking, and negotiated rate cards, contracts, and SLAs.

● Drive freight cost optimization (15–20% opportunity) through consolidation, mode shift, lane redesign, packaging optimization, and duty-scheme utilization, with savings quantified and validated with Finance.

● Maintain a live shipment tracker, lead-time master, and logistics risk dashboard — lane, port, carrier, regulatory, and geopolitical exposure — with alternate routing and backup partners identified for every critical lane.

● Implement forwarder and CHA performance scorecards (on-time performance, clearance turnaround, documentation accuracy, damage rate, billing hygiene) and run quarterly business reviews.

● Manage cargo insurance coverage and drive damage, shortage, and loss claims to closure.

● Write and maintain SOPs, escalation matrices, and checklists; support the scale-up to 200 units per year without logistics appearing as a cause of build or deployment schedule slip.

Required Qualifications and Skills

● Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Supply Chain, Logistics, Commerce, or a related field.

● 4–8 years of experience in international logistics, freight forwarding, or shipper-side EXIM operations.

● Hands-on ownership of both import and export operations — not one side only — with demonstrated experience across all three modes: air, ocean, and in-land freight.

● Strong working knowledge of Indian customs procedure and documentation — bill of entry and shipping bill filing, HS classification, duty structure, ICEGATE, and Incoterms 2020.

● Proven track record of negotiating freight rates and managing forwarder, CHA, and transporter relationships across multiple lanes.

● Hands-on global lane exposure (mandatory exposure beyond India — China and US preferred).

● Working knowledge of trade compliance obligations — licences, registrations, product certification, and audit requirements.

● Ability to build and defend a freight and landed-cost model in Excel or Google Sheets, and to run the function from data rather than instinct.

● Clear written and verbal communication in English, with the confidence to escalate and negotiate with carriers, brokers, and customs authorities.

Preferred Experience

● Previous experience in logistics or EXIM at Automobiles, Electric Vehicles, Automation, Industrial Equipment, Capital Goods, Robotics, Drones, or Aerospace organizations.

● Experience shipping dangerous goods, particularly lithium-ion batteries, and handling over-dimensional or high-value cargo.

● Familiarity with duty-saving and bonded schemes — MOOWR, EPCG, Advance Authorisation, SEZ, or FTWZ operations.

● Exposure to China, Taiwan, South-East Asia, US, and EU trade lanes and their supplier ecosystems.

● Exposure to ERP or logistics management systems (SAP, Oracle, Zoho, Odoo, Tally) and shipment visibility platforms.

● Certification such as CHA, IATA DGR, CSCP, or an equivalent trade-compliance qualification.

● Comfortable with low-volume / high-mix shipping rhythm and startup environments where the process has to be built, not inherited.

Preferred Skills

● Freight rate benchmarking and negotiation

● Customs documentation and HS classification

● Multi-modal routing and mode-shift analysis

● Trade compliance and duty-scheme management

● Dangerous goods and export packaging standards

● Landed-cost and freight spend modeling

● Logistics risk management and contingency planning

● Vendor score carding and quarterly business reviews

● Strong Excel and data management skills
